//: THE TEST TREE'S TYPE PROGRAM — the guards are code, and until this file existed they
were the only code in the repository no compiler ever read.
`tsconfig.json` includes 'src/**/*.ts' + 'shared/**/*.ts' and `tsconfig.server.json`
includes 'server/**/*.ts' and EXCLUDES 'tests'. Measured with the compiler itself
(`tsc --listFilesOnly`): 661 files in the first program, 663 in the second, and ZERO
under tests/ in either. So every type-level promise a helper under tests/ makes was
erased with no diagnostic — a branded scan root, a required floor argument, a narrowed
return — and the guards enforcing every invariant in the repository were the least
type-protected code in it.
This file changes WHAT is checked, never HOW: the compiler options are inherited from
tsconfig.json so the tests are held to exactly the strictness the app is. `tests/**` is
named as a glob so membership is a fact about the FILESYSTEM, not about the import
graph — a helper nothing imports yet is checked exactly like one that everything does.
`server/**` is in the file set because ~a third of the guards import the server they
guard; without it their imports resolve to nothing and every symbol becomes `any`,
which is the erasure this file exists to end wearing a different hat.
vitest's globals (`describe`/`it`/`expect`/`vi`) are configured in vitest.config.ts
(`globals: true`), so the ambient declarations must be in `types` or every test file
is a wall of 'cannot find name' errors that say nothing about the code.
`npm run typecheck` includes this program through `npm run typecheck:tests`, alongside
include liveness, client, server and Svelte template checks. Keep these compiler
options strict and the discovered test population complete; a passing subset does
not certify the complete command. Historical first-run diagnostics remain in the
dated research and findings records.
